deferred_phases.name: Trust/Evidence Aggregation
deferred_phases.reason: Explicitly deferred per the spec's own conditional clause ('only if identity and evidence foundations are now strong enough... if implementation would be speculative or weak, explicitly defer this phase rather than creating fake trust infrastructure'). Investigated src/os/health.rs (stateless, point-in-time only, nothing accumulates) and os::supervisor's hash-chained receipt chain (halt()/unlock()/set_quarantine()/clear_quarantine() DO take a real, human-supplied actor parameter and hash-chain it -- genuine per-actor evidence exists). But that evidence is narrow: only 4 supervisor-safety-event categories, nothing about routine task outcomes. os::autonomy::QueuedAction (the one place with real Succeeded/Failed/RolledBack outcomes) has no actor field at all. Aggregating only halt/unlock/quarantine counts into a 'trust score' would produce a number that looks meaningful but reflects almost nothing about an actor's ordinary behavior -- an actor who never triggers a safety event would be indistinguishable from a perfectly-behaved one, exactly the vanity-metric failure this codebase's own 69-cognitive-reliability-law.md (L6.4/L6.5) warns against, and exactly what this phase's own text calls 'fake trust infrastructure.'
deferred_phases.prerequisite_work_not_yet_done: Actor attribution threaded into os::autonomy::QueuedAction (so routine automated-action outcomes become actor-attributed and aggregable) and lease-usage receipts logging each evaluate_for_actor decision per actor -- either would give a real, non-speculative behavioral trail beyond safety incidents. Neither exists today; inventing either just to unblock Phase 14 would itself be undeclared scope expansion into Phase 13's territory after the fact, not this phase's job.

architectural_decisions.decision: Found (via grep, then confirmed via `cargo build --features mcp`) that Cargo.toml's own `mcp` feature is a documented, intentional prototype-spike separate from `cli` ('Program J ... Research/Prototype spike ONLY -- not wired into any live client path, not part of default cli'). This single root cause explains the entire capability::{system,git,repo}/evidence::ToolEvidence dead-code cluster flagged throughout Phases 16-18 -- confirming, with the authoritative source, what those phases' own checkpoints had already (correctly, but only inferentially) concluded.
architectural_decisions.why: Phase 20 step 1 ('trace the full live execution path') and step 9 ('run complete project gates') both call for exactly this: not trusting a cli-only cargo test run as 'the' gate when a second, real client feature (mcp) exists. Running the mcp build confirmed Phase 16's capability::system::host_summary rewrite is correct under its REAL reachable path, not only under the build where it happened to be unreachable.

architectural_decisions.decision: Confirmed via grep that src/monitor/health.rs (HealthRegistry/ComponentHealth/HealthState/ServiceHealthSnapshot) exists solely to serve os::service::watchdog.rs -- extending the already-known 'os::service::* is dead code' finding to a second, separate top-level module. Both were investigated, named, and explicitly NOT deleted.
architectural_decisions.why: Phase 20 step 2 says 'remove dead abstractions and remove ONLY those proven unnecessary' -- 'not currently wired to a CLI command by this specific 20-phase spec' is a narrower claim than 'proven unnecessary.' os::service::* represents substantial, tested, safety-conscious infrastructure (governed argv-array spawn, secret-redacted attribution receipts, a real supervised-restart loop) that a separate, prior investigation this session found (in a since-discarded plan-mode artifact) explicitly intended to wire up later. Deleting several hundred lines of tested code is consequential and hard to reverse in spirit -- named for anh Tâm's explicit decision (wire it up or remove it) in the architecture doc update, not deleted unilaterally mid-autonomous-run.

architectural_decisions.decision: Confirmed clean, no fix needed: HALT authority (only os::supervisor writes GIAMTHI_HALT.lock; os::service::watchdog/runtime only read its existence, even though that code is otherwise dead), local-first behavior (zero real network calls in os::), and resource/model placement explainability (both PlacementDecision and ModelPlacementDecision carry a reasons: Vec<String> field, confirmed by reading the structs directly, with PlacementDecision's own doc comment stating it is 'the explainable half of deterministic explainable placement decision').
architectural_decisions.why: Phase 20 steps 3, 6, 7, 8 all ask for exactly this kind of verification. Reporting 'confirmed clean' with the grep/read evidence that produced that conclusion is itself the deliverable for a consolidation phase -- not everything a final review checks turns out to need a code change, and that is a legitimate, evidence-based outcome, not a shortcut.
